steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Phew—Zone 2 is finally all cleaned up, now it's just Zone 4 left. How are you doing? Tough work, eh? Want to take a break?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I'm cleaning just as fast as you are, as you can plainly see.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You don't need to try and accommodate me just because I'm an Infected.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: That's not it at all. I just thought you must be tired, with everything you've been through and all.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Oh, I thought... never mind. As for that incident with the crown, I'm fully clear on that now.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: It was just a spur-of-the-moment thing! Besides, you're not the only one who wanted to do that.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Actually, it seems like all of a sudden, people aren't as afraid of the Infected anymore.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: That's because we're in Londinium. The policies instituted by the Speaker and Parliament have, at the very least, stopped many people from openly showing fear and resentment towards the Infected.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: But according to a Columbian friend of mine, outside of Londinium, things haven't changed.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Anyway, thanks for helping with the cleanup; we would've had the captain on us again without you.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I should be the one thanking you for not shackling me. Having something to do helps put my mind at ease.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: If you ask me, you need not worry about Parliament's decision. Think about it. Of all the places in Londinium where they could have detained you, why did they choose the Defense Forces' lockup?

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: It's because we're all either old war buddies or familiar faces who can look out for you. Don't worry. Once things cool down, we'll find a reason for you to go home.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: The protestors outside the Speaker's office, they're the ones who are missing the picture. We all know what kind of person Vina is.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Hmm? Are you feeling alright? Do you need something to drink?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You're saying... the Speaker is going to release me?

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: I'm saying just rest here for now, where it's safe, until things die down out there.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: The captain didn't allow you to have a radio or read the newspaper, right? It's because he was worried that you might get to thinking too much.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: If you're still feeling jittery, my good buddy—he gets thrown in the drunk tank every few days—he's stashed some premium hooch around here somewhere.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: I'll go grab a few bottles for you.
Diane gives a faint, wry smile as she strains to catch the sounds coming from outside.
But aside from the faint sound of water running through pipes, she hears nothing but the distant drills of the Defense Forces.
Ever since she was brought in here, she has been more or less cut off from the outside world.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I wonder if Eliseo is doing alright?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I really should have let him know beforehand. He must be so worried about me now…
Indeed. He went to nearly everyone he knows to plead on your behalf.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Madam Speaker!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Good. They aren't treating you like some common criminal.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: And you made sure of that?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No. They did it on their own—they believe you don't deserve this sentence.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Many came to me on your behalf. Your friends, my friends… our comrades-in-arms, and even some civilians who don't know you at all.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: —Diane, I snatched some of my buddy's liquor for you.
He takes a big swig of whiskey.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Urk!
Before the soldier even reaches Diane and Vina, he snaps to attention, the whiskey caught awkwardly in his mouth—too afraid to swallow or spit it out.
He quickly hides the bottle behind him and salutes Vina.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Gulp!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No need to hide it, Patel.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: As I recall, Horn did mention that drinking is prohibited in the barracks.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: (Swallows) Uhh... ahem…

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Yes, Vina! But… this is… uh…

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I won't tell Horn, but in return, you'll keep my visiting Diane a secret.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: And set the bottle down, will you? Weren't you bringing it to Diane, anyway?

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: Uh… alright. Vina, you came here to discuss the plans with Diane, right?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: See, Diane? I told you not to worry, didn't I?

steps.name: Diligent Guard
steps.text: I'll go finish cleaning Zone 4. I've been on duty all day, and I didn't see anyone here.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Would you like a taste of the whiskey Patel left? It doesn't smell all that bad.
Diane shakes her head slightly, a bit downcast.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Mind if I have a sip, then? Meeting with those dukes has left me parched.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Madam Speaker, did you put me here because you really wanted to…?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: We thought you'd feel better among old friends. You would rather I threw you in solitary?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: No, of course not.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Honestly, I'm not as resolute as you think. My past isn't much different from yours, or from that of most Londiniers.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Diane, I did hesitate over my decision.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: So, does your visit mean Parliament has come to a verdict?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: (Sigh) I feel it best that I inform you of Parliament's decision in person.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I bid you adieu, Lieutenant Diane Weber of the former 6th Column, 10th Infantry Regiment. You are unquestionably a war hero.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Thank you for your great service to our homeland.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Parliament...? I see. Madam Speaker, when will it happen?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Tomorrow.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Have you any regrets?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Have you?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Perhaps my biggest regret is that, after the war, I didn't immediately strip off this outfit and hide myself away back in Norport.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Ha, you would never have done that. I know you. The Siege will never abandon our homeland, and the Speaker of Londinium will never abandon Victoria.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I have no regrets either, Vina—may I call you that?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You may.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: We've met many times and fought side by side just as often. But today, I think, is the first day we can truly call ourselves friends.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Vina, before I go, would you share a drink with me?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: When you walked alone into the Palace of Westhaleg, everyone believed that the woman who emerged would be wearing the crown.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: 'A hero must one day be crowned king.'

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Every collection of fairytales in that old bookstore on Baker Street had a story like that. It was my favorite place to go before I enlisted.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I really did want to witness history, Vina.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But I let you down. I let a lot of people down.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Yes... You could have been a great ruler.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Just because I wanted to make Londinium a better place? Didn't the old king, the one who was hanged public, also want to make Londinium, to make all of Victoria, a better place?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Things rarely go as planned.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sometimes, what you believe is right may look wrong to others. I've only recently begun to understand that.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Then what is there to do?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'm still searching for that answer, Diane.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Someone I trust told me to try to accept those who hate me and to stand firm in my own sense of justice…

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'm still learning… but I never imagined this path would be so lonely.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You're drunk… Vina.
Vina shakes her head. She draws her sword and hands it to Diane.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Do you remember Kyngasycath, the Sighs of Kings?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Yes. I took it from your own hands, after all.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: After the battle, I discovered that it had completely dulled. The smiths worked tirelessly, day and night, to reforge it for me.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: This new sword is heavier. It carries the weight of even greater expectations than before.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Diane, this sword reminds me every day of the right path—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The future of Victoria doesn't rest with me or Parliament. It rests on all of you—those who reclaimed our home with their own strength.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Vina, I have one last question.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: What really happened in the Palace of Westhaleg that day?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What kind of story would you like to hear?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: A heroic fairytale that'll make it into the books of that old bookstore, or the truth, so plain that it's almost boring?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Haha.
Diane takes a long swig of her drink, her hand brushing over the cold steel of the sword.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: To be honest, I prefer the old sword… When I used it to strike down our enemies, those were the moments I felt closest to Victoria.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Back when I was living a simple, uneventful life, I never imagined I'd have thoughts like these…

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: And besides, there's hardly any time left to savor those quiet, pre-war days, is there?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Vina, forgive me, but I can't save the last bit of this whiskey for you. I really need it—

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: (Choking up) Why now, of all times, am I suddenly afraid to die?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: (Choking back tears) Vina, before I'm completely drunk, would you tell me one last fairytale?
Her tears fall on the sword, sliding down its blade. 'Drip', 'drip'...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Diane… you already know the stories of the past, and you were there for the best parts of this fairytale.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But you may not know how it ends.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: That day, I entered the Palace of Westhaleg, tore down the Sarkaz banner, and was about to leave—when suddenly, I heard someone call my name from the throne room.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: 'Alexandrina Vina Victoria.'

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Then I pushed open the door that had been sealed for so long.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I saw—
my father. Alistair II, speaking to me.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: My Alexandrina! You're finally home.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Come sit by my side, daughter of Victoria.
Vina couldn't make out the King's face.
The golden mask blended with his golden hair, radiating authority and an air of mystery.
He was Victoria personified.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: My daughter, are you afraid of me? Are you afraid of Victoria?

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Vina, never reveal even the slightest hint of fear to your subjects. Your teacher should have taught you that.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You died long ago.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Twenty-six years ago, they hanged you from the gallows.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Laughable! Who could kill Victoria?!

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Those greedy condorwings thought they could tear the flesh from my body to feed themselves.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: They were so blinded by fear that they conspired in regicide, all so they could feast upon the lands of the Aslans for their own gain.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: But no one can kill us—not the dukes, not the Red Dragon. We are the beating heart of Victoria!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So that's why… your statue in the Mausoleum of Kings was never completed…

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The dukes never truly laid you to rest; you've been here all along.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: What little courage they possessed drove them to confine me in this throne room, but never to claim my throne. Cowardly usurpers!

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: They fear my people; they fear my Steam Knights; they fear us, Vina.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: My daughter, tell me, do my people still remember me? Do my knights still guard our palace?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The people of Victoria have long since adapted to life without a monarch. As for your knights, they're all gone.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: They were murdered by the very people they were sworn to protect.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: And what of you, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I… I can barely remember what you look like.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Then come closer. Take off my mask and look closely… you'll see only yourself, Alexandrina. The blood of the royal line flows in us both.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: I'm sorry, my child, that I failed to keep my promise.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: I intended to hand you a peaceful and powerful Victoria, yet betrayal has left me sitting here, rotting on my throne, for over twenty years.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: But at last, you've returned. Take my scepter, wear my crown…

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Proclaim to our people that their sovereign has returned.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Purge our land of all dissent and punish every coward who betrayed the crown. Let glory endure—this is Victoria's rightful way!
The king's scepter struck heavily against the throne platform, its dull echo reverberating.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: …Blood was never the source of our strength.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: How familiar those words are—just like my defiant boasts to my own father.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: (Chuckles) You still have much to learn, my daughter. Let me teach you a long-overdue lesson: the meaning of 'royal power'!

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Still, I grant you the right to oppose me.

steps.name: Alistair II
steps.text: Alexandrina, return to my side, and listen.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No. You're already dead, Your Majesty. All that remains here is your echo, lost in the glories of a bygone empire.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I do not need you to grant me anything, nor do I need you to validate the strength of my convictions.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...I just want you to rest in peace, Father.
Vina tightened her grip on her hammer, stepped onto the platform, and walked toward the Empire's last glimmer of twilight.
